definitions.explanation: The number three thousand. Note the sound change: さん + せん becomes さんぜん (the せ becomes voiced to ぜ).

examples.japanese: この{時計|とけい}は{三千|さんぜん}{円|えん}でした。
examples.english: This watch was three thousand yen.

examples.japanese: {三千|さんぜん}{人|にん}が{参加|さんか}しました。
{富士山|ふじさん}は{三千|さんぜん}メートル{以上|いじょう}あります。
examples.english: Mt. Fuji is over three thousand meters tall.

examples.japanese: この{町|まち}には{三千|さんぜん}{年|ねん}の{歴史|れきし}があります。とても{古|ふる}い{町|まち}です。
examples.english: This town has three thousand years of history. It's a very old town.

notes: Three thousand has a sound change where せん becomes ぜん. This is called rendaku (sequential voicing). Similarly, {八千|はっせん} (8000) has a different change where the reading becomes はっせん. Other thousands (2000, 4000, 5000, 6000, 7000, 9000) keep the regular せん sound.
